prize_parts.citation: For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, enabling measurement of time and frequency at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: After reading the full set of opening ballots I move B027 to the head of my own list. It is the only shortlisted candidate that seven of eight members rank, five of them in the top three, and on reading the assessments that breadth is backed by substance rather than by mere comfort. The magic-wavelength lattice removes Doppler and recoil shifts while retaining a large atom number, which is a genuine new regime of control, not an incremental improvement. It has delivered clocks at the 1e-18 level, reproduced and compared across JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others, and it supports gravitational redshift tests over millimetre scales, constraints on variation of constants and the coming redefinition of the second. The discovery is the control scheme and its demonstrated performance, not only the application. Attribution is the cleanest on the list: Katori for the magic-wavelength idea and first strontium lattice clock, Ye for taking it to record accuracy and for the many-body clock physics. Two names leave room under the three-person limit and every member who proposed laureates named exactly this pair.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is overlap with prior metrology prizes: the 2005 prize (Hall, Hansch) for combs and the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) for single-quantum-system control and ion clocks. A committee could judge that the field of optical frequency standards has been rewarded twice already, and that the lattice clock is the application of earlier discoveries rather than a new one. There is also the practical point that the SI second has not yet been redefined, and others (Lemonde, Ludlow, Oates, Takamoto) are outside the credited names. I weigh these as real but insufficient, since the magic-wavelength scheme and many-body clock physics are distinct inventions.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B027 first as the clearest case of a technique that changed what can be measured, and ranks my own B036 seventh because the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize makes the timing delicate.
responses.response: I agree on both points and it moves me. I opened with circuit QED first, but I should not let proximity to my own field and to the programme I direct outweigh the point that the 2025 prize has just rewarded the macroscopic-quantum foundation of this area. Recognising cQED one year later would look like a second prize in a single field, whereas the clock is far from that. Where I would qualify your view is the claim that the lattice clock is clearly separate from earlier frequency prizes: I would still want the citation to name the magic-wavelength lattice and its demonstrated accuracy explicitly, so that it does not read as a comb or ion-clock prize extended.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B027 first because Lamb-Dicke trapping with cancelled light shifts turns an atomic-structure insight into a new level of precision, and notes the 2005 and 2012 prizes can be read as precedent either for or against.
responses.response: As a non-specialist in atomic structure I find that framing persuasive: the point is that the cancellation of light shifts is itself the discovery, and it is not a combination of known tools. On the precedent question I think it cuts mildly for us, since the 2005 and 2012 prizes made the clock possible but neither covers neutral atoms trapped in a lattice. I disagree gently with the suggestion to widen the credit to Zoller or comb-clock coupling; that would blur a clean pair and Zoller already appears in B060 and B006, so double-counting is a concern.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B053 first on aberration correction, which broke the Scherzer limit and is in routine use worldwide, and ranks B027 second while warning recognition might be premature before the SI second redefinition.
responses.response: I take B053 seriously as an instrument breakthrough with huge downstream use, and your declaration of closeness to the field is exactly the standard I try to apply to myself on B036. My reservation is only that I cannot judge the Krivanek priority question, which both you and Pearce flag, and a disputed three-name credit worries me more than the redefinition timing for B027. I do not think the second needs to be redefined first: the physics is established by many independent comparisons at 1e-18, and the prize would be for the invention, not for the redefinition.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B057 first as a clear verified discovery of a new class of quantum matter, with Kane and Mele for theory and Molenkamp for experiment, and ranks B027 fifth.
responses.response: Topological insulators are outside my expertise, so I defer on the physics, and I accept that this is a major conceptual advance. My concern is attribution rather than merit: several ballots, including yours, note that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction and the 3D work are outside the credited trio, and the 2016 topology prize forces the committee to explain what is added. If the credit question for B057 can be settled in the committee's favour I would see it as a leading rival to B027, and I would rank it above B036 in my own order.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will read the lattice clock as distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, which I believe is the deciding issue for B027.
Whether the credit for B057 can be cleanly resolved without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, which I cannot judge from the supplied names.
Whether B060 should be framed as the Cirac-Zoller proposal plus Blatt, or as a theory-only prize, given the 2012 Wineland prize.
statement.conflict_note: I direct the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and work on superconducting circuit QED at Chalmers, and Chalmers has hosted 2025 laureates as guest researchers, so I have a clear connection to B036 and some to B060 as a quantum-computing platform. I should recuse myself or at least weigh my vote with care on B036. I have no specific connection apparent from my profile to B027, B053, B057, B041, B008, B032, B040, B047 or B006.
